SETTING (blocks 60, 67, 71 of the source-link direction; open PRs #8590, #8598, #8603; supplied clauses, not adopted; read those three notes on their PR branches before starting). Block 60's curvature member, bodies at rest in a box with held walls: chi = 1 + sum Q_i g_i, Q_i chi_i = m_i/(8K), ledger = 8K sum Q. Block 67 T1: when a spread amplitude at rest (charges Q_x) is replaced by ONE record at site y, the ledger is kept iff the record's charge is Q' = sum_x Q_x, i.e. its bare energy is m' = 8K Q'(1 + Q' g_yy); for positive amplitudes this is always possible (the ledger of one site is unbounded). Block 71 T3: a negative body at rest has a static field with positive rates iff its charge lies on the admissible branch, Q > -1/(2 g_0), equivalently m > -2K/g_0; at the bound the unit-source potential is a zero mode of -Delta + Q/chi. RULES: nothing is adopted; no rule of formation is assumed; identities in arbitrary odds; the parked statistical postulate in docs/repo/DEFERRED_DECISIONS.md is neither used nor approached; exact arithmetic or clearly labelled floating point. TASK: the supervisor's observation, not in any note: combining block 67 T1(a) with block 71 T3, a spread amplitude of NEGATIVE energy has a ledger-keeping record at site y iff sum_x Q_x > -1/(2 g_yy) - a threshold where positive amplitudes have none. (a) Prove or refute it: check that a spread negative amplitude with each Q_x on its own admissible branch can have sum Q_x below -1/(2 g_yy) (give an exact example on a small box: several sites, exact rational g), that its own static field exists with positive rates (block 71 T3(d)'s criterion: -Delta + Q/chi positive definite with walls held), and that then no single record keeps the ledger. (c) Two or more records: how many sites are needed to keep the ledger, as a function of sum Q? (d) State what this asymmetry between the signs means for the owner's fork 'which amplitudes are present' without proposing any rule. HIT if a spread negative amplitude below the threshold nevertheless has a ledger-keeping single record, or if the amplitude in (a) has no static field of its own.
